newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Short Australian debt futures break out.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Short Australian debt futures break out.

text.p: *Australian three-year bond and bill futures broke out of the top side of their recent ranges in after hours trading amid talk that a further interest rate cut was still on the cards.
*Ten-year bonds futures also outperformed the U.S., which closed lower amid a lack of data ahead of its holiday weekend.

Australian three-year bond and bill futures broke out of the top side of their recent ranges in after hours trading amid speculation that a further official interest rate cut was still on the cards, traders said.

The June bill contract touched its highest level in a month at 94.16 at one stage before closing SYCOM at 94.14 and up from Thursday's 94.07 pit close. The close equated to a cash rate of 5.86 percent compared with official rates of 6.0 percent.
The break of 94.12 on the contract sets up a move for a test of 94.18 and then a more rigid band of resistance at 94.21/94.23, analysts said.

An article in the Australian Financial Review suggesting Thursday's downward revision in the first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) set the stage for an easing added fire to recent speculation, and knocked the Australian dollar back in offshore trading.
The first quarter AWOTE revision took the annual rate down to 4.3 percent from 4.6 percent and back below the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent "line in the sand".
Comments by Treasury Secretary Ted Evans on Thursday were also being viewed as arguing for a rate cut at the next Reserve Bank board meeting on June 3.
